name: Sporza
discovery: Not advertised: there are no feed <link> tags, no RSS page, and no 'rss' string in the sporza.be HTML or JS. The site is a React Router v7 SSR app. The feeds were found by applying VRT's AEM selector pattern. The homepage feed is https://sporza.be/nl.rss.xml (any selector after .rss gives the same result). Category feeds are https://sporza.be/nl/categorie/<path>.rss.xml for any category on the A-Z page https://sporza.be/nl/a-z/ (about 200 /nl/categorie/ paths). Every category path tested worked. Tag pages (/nl/tag/...) have no feed. Sitemaps were found via robots.txt. All streams are therefore official=false.

apis.name: Google News sitemap (nl)
apis.purpose: The only CHRONOLOGICAL 'latest' list for Sporza (all RSS feeds are in editorial order). Use it to fill a 'meest recent' stream or to backfill timestamps; titles only.
apis.responseNotes: <urlset> with 85 <url> elements covering about 2 days. Each has loc (canonical article URL /nl/YYYY/MM/DD/<slug>~<id>/), news:publication_date with a local Belgian offset (range 2026-10-23T17:02:16+02:00 to 2026-10-25T15:48:56+01:00) and news:title. No images, no summaries, no sport label (derive it from the slug or by joining with feed ids).
apis.freshness: Live (the newest entry matched the newest RSS entry).

apis.name: Sitemap index (nl)
apis.purpose: Discovery of article sitemaps per sport and per week, for backfill or category discovery.
apis.notes: No clean JSON API exists. api.sporza.be (the BFF in window.ENV) returns 403 or 404 for every guessed route. The page data is embedded only as a React Router turbo-stream in the SSR HTML, which is not reported (that would be HTML scraping).

quirks:
Feeds are Atom (application/feed+xml, xml:lang nl) behind CloudFront with cache-control max-age=60. Some origin responses on a cache miss are slow (two fetches timed out at 20 s and succeeded on retry), so use a 30 s timeout plus one retry. The feed <title> is always 'sporza' and the feed <author> is 'sporza - Vrt', even for category feeds. The feed self link is WRONG on every feed (always https://sporza.be/nl/.rss.xml), so key streams by the requested URL, not the self link.
Max 20 entries per feed (some have 9-15). Order is EDITORIAL (the page layout), NOT chronological: hero articles come first, then a block of video items. Sort by <updated> yourself. The homepage feed covers only about 7.5 hours.
Entry fields: title (type=text), id (= canonical URL, not a short link), published, updated, summary type=text, vrtns:nstag, link rel=alternate, link rel=enclosure (image). No <author>, <category> or <content>. The content namespace is declared but never used.
Video items: in many category feeds 4-11 of 20 entries have 'video' (and often 'Sporzatips') in nstag. Their summary is usually EMPTY, which is why summary coverage drops to 'some'. Decide whether to show them (they link to the video article page).
nstag is a PIPE-SEPARATED list: sport|competition|teams|people|editor names|'video'. Example: 'voetbal|Jupiler Pro League|KRC Genk|Standard|voetbal|Joël Heymbeeck'. It contains duplicates and inconsistent case and accents (e.g. 'Formule 1|autosport|Formule 1|autosport'). Split it, dedupe case-insensitively, take the first token as the sport, and drop editor names (they are not distinguishable from player names, so do not use it as author).
Link patterns:
- articles: /nl/YYYY/MM/DD/<slug>~<numeric id>/
- match pages: /nl/matches/<sport>/<competition>/<season>/.../<slug>~<id>/ (these update in place: title, summary and updated change during and after the match)
- evergreen category landing pages: /nl/categorie/... (e.g. Olympics hubs dated 2021-2023 in andere-sporten). Filter these out.
Titles prefixed 'LIVE' or 'LIVESTREAM' are live items. The date in the URL is the original creation date and can differ from <published> (e.g. /2026/10/12/ for an item published 2026-10-25), so do not parse dates from URLs. Dates are UTC with milliseconds ('2026-10-25T14:32:45.741Z').
Dedupe across streams by <id> (= URL): parent and child categories overlap heavily (auto-motor/formule-1 60%, zaalsport/basketbal 60%, tour/wegwielrennen 60% with identical first 5 off-season).
Images: every entry has an enclosure https://images.vrt.be/width1280/YYYY/MM/DD/<uuid>.jpg (image/jpeg). The preset segment can be swapped (orig, width640, width320, w960hx, w640hx, w480hx, w1280hx, vrtnws_share).
No premium or paywall: Sporza is free (VRT public broadcaster), so premium=false always. No tracking params.
Category URL rule: any /nl/categorie/<path>/ page from https://sporza.be/nl/a-z/ (about 200 paths, including per-competition ones like voetbal/buitenland/dfb-pokal, zaalsport/basketbal/wnba, wielrennen/wegwielrennen/wk-wielrennen) has a feed at https://sporza.be/nl/categorie/<path>.rss.xml. Validate a non-empty atom body because non-categories return HTML with 200.
robots.txt disallows / for named AI crawlers (ClaudeBot, GPTBot, etc.) while allowing User-agent *. Fetch politely with a normal UA, at most once a minute (matches max-age=60).

gapNotes: I re-fetched all 46 reported Sporza URLs on 2026-10-25: every one returned 200 with valid Atom (application/feed+xml). Only one exact duplicate exists, tour/wegwielrennen (see remove). Other pairs overlap partly but are distinct streams: auto-motor/formule-1 (12/20), basketbal/zaalsport (12/20), mountainbike/onverhard (6/20, 4 of the first 5 shared). Fresh counts that differ from the report: home, voetbal, jupiler-pro-league, veldrijden, voetbal-buitenland, voetbal-nederland, voetbal-engeland and tennis each have 20 entries, with the newest at about 15:10 to 15:24Z.

Borderline freshness among the reported streams. voetbal-frankrijk: newest item 2026-10-12, 13 days old even in mid-season. I kept it because it is just under the 14-day threshold, but make it default-off or fold it into voetbal-buitenland. Also slow: zwemmen (newest 10-17, 8 days), golf (10-18), croky-cup (10-21). Some feeds carry old evergreen entries: andere-sporten has a 2021 entry, motogp a 2020 one, and wegwielrennen's oldest is from 2022. Sort by <updated> and cap item age in the client.

Completeness: I fetched every category on the A-Z page (163 paths, including X2o-trofee-veldrijden, whose path has an uppercase X) and kept only the 9 additions. Rejected:
- Empty landing pages with 0 entries: formule-1-grand-prix-kalender, formule-1-stand-wk-2026, the tennis ATP/WTA kalender and ranglijst pages, veldrijden-kalender, wegwielrennen/kalender, worldtourranking.
- Duplicate: andere-sporten/watersport has the same first 5 entries as zwemmen.
- Event subsets: wk-turnen, ek/wk-kunstschaatsen, tennis/european-open (20 fresh items, but the tournament ends today; seasonal for October).
- Too thin (1 item in 14 days): gewichtheffen, korfbal, triatlon, zaalvoetbal, black-arrows, ek-atletiek, champions-league-volleybal, uefa-youth-league, yellow-tigers, belgian-cats, boksen (vechtsport covers it), skeeleren, motorcross, skateboard, taekwondo, wk-voetbal-2026, diamond-league, 3x3-basketbal.

- voetbal/vrouwen/women-super-league: the site labels it 'Lotto Women's Pro League' (Belgian league, not the English WSL). Not added: only 2 items in 14 days and 6 of 20 ids shared with vrouwenvoetbal.

Fetch reliability: 5 of 163 category fetches timed out at 25 s on a cache miss (kunstschaatsen/ek-kunstschaatsen, tennis/australian-open-1, tennis/davis-cup, tennis/european-open, olympische-spelen voetbal) and all succeeded on immediate retry. This confirms the existing quirk: use a 30 s timeout plus one retry. All 9 additions come from the same /nl/categorie/<path>.rss.xml pattern. They share the existing quirks: editorial order, max 20 entries, feed <title> always 'sporza', wrong self link, image in link[rel=enclosure], and nstag as a pipe-separated category list.
